svg.text: One sinusoid per dimension, wavelengths in geometric progression
pos is the position, i indexes the dimension.
Wavelengths run from 2 pi up to 10000 times 2 pi.

a.data-tiphead: Why any positional signal is needed
a.data-tip: Attention is a set operation: permute the input rows and the output rows permute with them. Since the model contains no recurrence and no convolution, order has to be injected explicitly.
a.text: Why a positional signal is needed at all
The model contains no recurrence and no convolution, so
nothing in it knows the order of the tokens. The encodings
have the same width as the embeddings, d_model = 512, and
are simply added to them at the bottom of both stacks.
Chosen so that for any fixed offset k, the encoding at
pos + k is a linear function of the encoding at pos.

a.data-tip: Table 3 row E swaps the sinusoids for learned positional embeddings and reports 4.92 perplexity and 25.7 BLEU against 4.92 and 25.8 for the base model. The choice was not made on accuracy.
a.text: Why sinusoids rather than learned embeddings
The paper tried both. Table 3 row E replaces the sinusoids
with learned positional embeddings and gets 4.92 PPL and
25.7 BLEU, against 4.92 and 25.8 for the base model:
The stated reason for choosing sinusoids is extrapolation:
they may let the model handle sequences longer than any

a.data-tip: The extrapolation argument is a hypothesis in the paper, not a measurement. No experiment in the paper tests sequences longer than those seen in training.
a.text: What the paper does not show
Extrapolation to longer sequences is the stated motive, but no experiment in the paper measures it.
Row E establishes only that the two options score the same on sequences of the kind seen in training.
